claims.text: Authors: Wei, J., Sun, Z., Papay, S., McKinney, S., Han, J., Fulford, I., Chung, H.
Research Problem: Existing benchmarks for web browsing agents lack challenging problems requiring extensive browsing and strategic reasoning.
Methodology: The authors introduced an inverted question design methodology, starting with answers and creating questions that are hard to find but easy to verify.
The benchmark comprises 1,266 challenging problems requiring persistent web navigation.
Novel benchmark design with inverted question methodology
Large-scale dataset (1,266 questions) for evaluating browsing agents
Comprehensive evaluation framework measuring multiple dimensions of browsing capability
Results: Deep Research achieved approximately 50% accuracy, significantly outperforming all other models (GPT-4o with browsing: 1.9%, GPT-4o without browsing: 0.6%).
Performance scaled with test-time compute, and best-of-N voting improved performance by 15-25%.
Limitations: Models with browsing capabilities exhibited higher calibration error (overconfident in incorrect answers).
Fourteen percent of tasks had 0% pass rate even for Deep Research.
Authors: Zhou, P., Leon, B., Ying, X., Zhang, C., Shao, Y., Ye, Q., Chong, D., Jin, Z., Xie, C., Cao, M., Gu, Y., Hong, S., Ren, J., Chen, J., Liu, C., & Hua, Y.
Research Problem: Existing benchmarks focus on English-language environments, lacking evaluation of LLM web browsing capabilities in the Chinese information environment.
Methodology: Reverse-design methodology with two-stage quality control.
The dataset comprises 289 high-quality question-answer pairs across 11 diverse domains.
First Chinese-language web browsing benchmark
Rigorous quality control pipeline ensuring difficulty and answer uniqueness
Comprehensive evaluation across 20+ models and AI search products
Results: Naive LLMs performed poorly (GPT-4o: 6.2%, Qwen2.5-72B: 6.6%).
Reasoning-enhanced models improved (O1: 29.1%, Gemini-2.5-Pro: 27.3%).
Agentic systems with multi-turn retrieval dominated (DeepResearch: 42.9%, Doubao Deep Search: 26.0%).
Limitations: Small dataset size (289 questions) limits representativeness.
Answer uniqueness cannot be fully guaranteed despite rigorous validation.
Authors: Wu, J., Yin, W., Jiang, Y., Wang, Z., Xi, Z., Fang, R., Zhang, L., He, Y., Zhou, D., Xie, P., & Huang, F.
Research Problem: Existing benchmarks lack evaluation of LLMs' ability to perform deep, vertical exploration in web-based information-seeking tasks.
Methodology: Dataset construction with 680 question-answer pairs across 4 domains (60.5% Chinese, 39.5% English).
Tasks involve traversing website hierarchies to depths of 2-8 levels.
WebWalkerQA benchmark for evaluating web traversal abilities
WebWalker multi-agent framework (Explorer + Critic agents)
Demonstration that RAG combined with WebWalker improves performance
Results: Closed-source models outperformed open-source models.
WebWalker framework outperformed baselines (WebWalker > Reflexion > ReAct).
Best performance (WebWalker with GPT-4o) remained below 40% accuracy.
Limitations: Maximum 15 actions for explorer agent limits exploration depth.
Context limitations affect model performance on long-horizon tasks.
Authors: Du, M., Xu, B., Zhu, C., Wang, X., & Mao, Z.
Research Problem: No comprehensive benchmark exists for evaluating deep research agents' report generation and web retrieval capabilities against authentic user needs.
Methodology: Derived from 96,147 real user queries, filtered to 44,019 deep research tasks, then expert-curated to 100 high-quality tasks across 22 domains.
Introduced two evaluation frameworks: RACE (report quality) and FACT (citation trustworthiness).
First comprehensive benchmark for Deep Research Agents with 100 tasks across 22 domains
Real-world grounding from 96k+ actual user queries
Dual evaluation framework: RACE for report quality, FACT for citation trustworthiness
Results: Gemini-2.5-Pro Deep Research led overall RACE performance.
OpenAI Deep Research showed strong instruction-following.
Gemini-2.5-Pro achieved 111.21 average effective citations.
Limitations: Resource-intensive evaluation requiring significant computational resources.
Commercial product opacity limits transparency of iteration cycles.
Authors: Li, X., Jin, J., Dong, G., Qian, H., Wu, Y., Wen, J.-R., Zhu, Y., & Dou, Z.
Research Problem: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) lack autonomous deep research capabilities for complex information-seeking tasks.
Methodology: Two-mode framework: (1) Problem-Solving Mode with Deep Web Explorer for autonomous search and navigation, (2) Report Generation Mode with Think-Search-and-Draft strategy.
RL-based training with iterative online DPO.
Training-free WebThinker framework for empowering LRMs
Deep Web Explorer component for autonomous web navigation
Think-Search-and-Draft strategy for report generation
Results: Outperformed Search-o1 by 21.9% on GAIA and 36.2% on HLE.
WebThinker-32B-RL achieved +8.5% on GAIA, +21.5% on HLE over base version.
Surpassed o3-mini (High) on HLE benchmark.
Limited tool set (search and basic navigation only).
Context window constraints for long trajectories.
Authors: Li, K., Zhang, Z., Yin, H., Zhang, L., Ou, L., Wu, J., Yin, W., Li, B., Tao, Z., Wang, X., Shen, W., Zhang, J., Zhang, D., Wu, X., Jiang, Y., Yan, M., Xie, P., Huang, F., & Zhou, J.
Research Problem: Open-source web agents exhibit near-zero accuracy on BrowseComp while proprietary systems achieve superhuman performance.
Methodology: Uncertainty-driven training data synthesis through random walks across interconnected knowledge structures.
Three-level task classification (Level 1-3).
Training pipeline: RFT cold start followed by DUPO (Duplicating Sampling Policy Optimization) for RL.
Uncertainty-driven training data synthesis (SailorFog-QA)
DUPO algorithm for efficient RL training (2-3x speedup over DAPO)
Results: WebSailor-7B achieved 6.7% on BrowseComp-en (outperforming 32B models).
WebSailor-72B matched proprietary Doubao performance.
Outperformed all open-source models and agentic methods.
Limitations: Context window cap (<32k tokens) limits complex problem handling.
Over-thinking tendency on simple questions.
Training efficiency limited to 50 steps due to synchronous framework.
Authors: Wu, J., Li, B., Fang, R., Yin, W., Zhang, L., Tao, Z., Zhang, D., Xi, Z., Fu, G., Jiang, Y., Xie, P., Huang, F., & Zhou, J.
Research Problem: Building autonomous information-seeking agents requires high-quality browsing data, reliable trajectories for long-horizon reasoning, and scalable training strategies.
Methodology: Four-stage pipeline: (1) browsing data construction (crawlQA + e2hQA), (2) trajectory sampling, (3) SFT for cold start, (4) RL with DAPO algorithm.
ReAct framework with two tools (search, click).
Scalable QA data synthesis methods (crawlQA + e2hQA)
Two-stage training pipeline (SFT + on-policy RL)
WebDancer agent achieving strong benchmark performance
Results: Surpassed GPT-4o on GAIA and WebWalkerQA benchmarks.
Agentic approaches built on reasoning-specialized models (QwQ-32B) consistently outperformed non-agentic counterparts.
Limitations: Limited to two basic tools (search, click).
Focuses only on short-answer tasks.
RL scalability constrained to 5,000 pairs due to computational limits.
Authors: Qiao, Z., Chen, G., Chen, X., Yu, D., Yin, W., Wang, X., Zhang, Z., Li, B., Yin, H., Li, K., Min, R., Liao, M., Jiang, Y., Xie, P., Huang, F., & Zhou, J.

Research Problem: Current mono-contextual deep-research systems suffer from cognitive workspace suffocation and irreversible noise contamination due to accumulating all information in a single context window.
Methodology: IterResearch paradigm reformulates deep research as a Markov Decision Process with periodic consolidation.
State structure: Question + evolving Report + latest Action/Observation.
WebFrontier data engine with three-stage iterative workflow.
IterResearch: Iterative paradigm preventing context suffocation and noise contamination
WebFrontier: Scalable data synthesis engine with tool-augmented complexity escalation
Research-Synthesis Framework for test-time scaling through parallel multi-agent exploration
Results: Achieved 36.7% on HLE (surpassing DeepSeek-V3.1: 29.8%, OpenAI Deep Research: 26.6%).
GAIA: 72.8% (surpassing all evaluated systems).
BrowseComp-en: 51.7% (matching OpenAI Deep Research: 51.5%).
Limitations: Computational cost increases linearly with parallel trajectories.
Architectural complexity compared to mono-contextual approaches.
Dependencies on external tools with potential rate limits.
Authors: Jin, B., Zeng, H., Yue, Z., Yoon, J., Arik, S., Wang, D., Zamani, H., & Han, J.
Research Problem: LLMs need to learn how to effectively interleave reasoning with search engine calls during inference.
Methodology: RL framework with special tokens (‹search›, ‹information›, ‹think›, ‹answer›).
Key innovation: retrieved token masking optimizes only LLM-generated tokens, not retrieved content.
Simple outcome-based reward function compatible with PPO and GRPO.
First RL framework for training LLMs to interleave reasoning with search
Retrieved token masking technique for efficient optimization
Simple outcome-based reward design (no complex reward engineering)
Results: 41% average relative improvement with Qwen2.5-7B over baselines. 20% improvement with Qwen2.5-3B.
Consistent gains across in-distribution and out-of-distribution datasets.
Outperformed RAG, IRCoT, Search-o1 across all datasets.
Limitations: Limited to QA tasks (not tested on open-ended research).
Fixed number of retrieved passages (3).
Only uses Wikipedia corpus (2018 dump).
RL training can be slow for complex multi-turn interactions.
Authors: Tao, Z., Wu, J., Yin, W., Zhang, J., Li, B., Shen, H., Li, K., Zhang, L., Wang, X., Jiang, Y., Xie, P., Huang, F., & Zhou, J.
Research Problem: Existing information-driven approaches for synthesizing training data suffer from structural inconsistencies, limited controllability, poor diversity, and reasoning shortcuts.
Methodology: Set theory-based mathematical formalization with Knowledge Projections (KP) for precise control over reasoning structures.
Agentic Expander with layer-wise expansion strategy.
Generated 18k seed questions → 5k high-quality trajectories.
Paradigm-shifting formalization-driven framework for data synthesis
Knowledge Projections enabling precise control over task complexity
Agentic Expander with layer-wise expansion avoiding redundancy and shortcuts
Results: Achieved state-of-the-art results on GAIA and WebWalkerQA benchmarks among open-sourced methods.
Demonstrated superior controllability compared to previous methods.
Focus on advantages and future directions.
